Diagnosis.submission: The faulty component is the frontend-proxy deployment in the astronomy-shop namespace. It has been replaced/tampered with (annotation edge.platform/change-ticket: EDGE-1847): the legitimate Envoy-based frontend-proxy (ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.2.0-frontend-proxy running its default entrypoint) was overridden to run a custom Perl "edge request filter / WAF" script. That script extracts a user-controlled query parameter (waf=...) and evaluates it against the regular expression ^([a-zA-Z]+)*$ via Perl. This pattern is a classic catastrophic-backtracking (ReDoS) regex: a long run of letters followed by a non-letter causes exponential backtracking, pinning the CPU. The load generator passes ~5001-character waf= candidates, and the frontend-proxy logs show each such request spending ~1 second in regex evaluation; with the container CPU limit of 100m this throttles/stalls the proxy, adding seconds of latency and degrading/blocking the storefront through the edge proxy. Root cause: a vulnerable, injected WAF regex in the modified frontend-proxy deployment, triggered by user-supplied waf= input causing catastrophic backtracking (ReDoS) and CPU exhaustion.
